description: Deterministic long-lived showcase capture for PcapFlowLab v1 materialization pass. Uses a single classic Ethernet PCAP timeline with overlapping hero flows, application demos, protocol-family coverage, grouping identity cases, and edge scenarios.

scenarios.name: Bulk TLS analysis hero
scenarios.purpose: Strongest Analysis demo with TLS, SNI, rate phases, bursts, idle gap, pagination, and byte asymmetry.
notes: Hero flow intentionally spans multiple rate phases over ~45 seconds.

scenarios.name: IPv6 interactive TCP analysis hero
scenarios.purpose: IPv6 generic TCP/Data flow with packet-balanced but byte-skewed traffic and visible ACK-only packets.
notes: Payload bytes are opaque and deterministic to avoid accidental HTTP/TLS detection.

scenarios.name: VLAN telemetry UDP analysis hero
scenarios.purpose: Non-TCP Analysis demo with VLAN path metadata and recurring telemetry packet sizes.
notes: Telemetry uses deterministic small, medium, large, and near-MTU payload sizes.

scenarios.name: Nested GRE/TLS analysis hero
scenarios.purpose: Complex protocol-path analysis hero with VLAN, stacked MPLS, GRE, inner TCP, and TLS/SNI.
scenarios.expected_protocol_path: EthernetII -> VLAN(vid=320) -> MPLS(label=16010) -> MPLS(label=16011) -> IPv4 -> GRE -> IPv4 -> TCP
notes: Both directions intentionally preserve the same VLAN/MPLS identifiers to avoid accidental flow split.

scenarios.name: Large captured packet size demo (~2.5 KB)
scenarios.purpose: Short UDP flow with exact large captured records around 2.5 KB for Analysis min/avg/max and capture packet-size distribution coverage.
notes: Synthetic large/offload-style captured records with caplen == origlen on the maximum packet.
EDGE-SNAPLEN-01 remains the separate truncated-capture example.

scenarios.name: Large captured packet size demo (~7.5 KB)
scenarios.purpose: Short UDP flow with one exact ~7.5 KB captured record for large-bucket statistics and per-flow size analysis.
notes: Synthetic large/offload-style captured records with caplen == origlen on the maximum packet.
No detected application protocol is expected.

scenarios.name: Large captured packet size demo (~60 KB)
scenarios.purpose: Short UDP flow with very large captured records up to ~60 KB to exercise capture-wide maximum packet handling and upper packet-size buckets.
notes: Synthetic jumbo/offload-style captured records with caplen == origlen on the maximum packet.
This scenario is intentionally unfragmented; EDGE-FRAG-01 remains the fragment example.

scenarios.name: Structured HTTP request/response
scenarios.purpose: Short IPv4 HTTP flow showing structured HTTP Stream behavior.

scenarios.name: Structured HTTP POST request/response
scenarios.purpose: Second short HTTP flow showing another confirmed HTTP/service case without introducing the later large-body scenario.
notes: Intentionally small; the dedicated large-body HTTP showcase remains a separate later pass.

scenarios.name: Large multi-packet HTTP response reassembly
scenarios.purpose: Clean in-order HTTP response whose body spans many normal-MTU TCP packets to exercise Stream reassembly, packet pagination, and Analysis byte dominance.
notes: Response headers intentionally remain in the first response data segment; only the body is segmented.
HTTP Stream Item Data currently remains unavailable by design because HTTP rows do not retain authoritative item-owned bytes.

scenarios.name: Structured DNS query/response with warning
scenarios.purpose: DNS flow with valid multi-answer behavior plus one truncated message warning.

scenarios.name: Structured DNS PTR query/response
scenarios.purpose: Second short DNS flow using PTR lookup semantics instead of another A/CNAME story.

scenarios.name: Structured mDNS / DNS-SD
scenarios.purpose: mDNS multicast discovery with PTR/SRV/TXT/A records.
notes: This scenario intentionally spans two multicast source flows while keeping one scenario ID.

scenarios.name: IPv6 mDNS / DNS-SD AAAA response
scenarios.purpose: Compact IPv6 UDP multicast mDNS / DNS-SD response with structured PTR, SRV, TXT, and AAAA presentation.

scenarios.name: Decryptable QUIC session from checked-in fixture
scenarios.purpose: Full checked-in QUIC session preserving exact protected UDP payload bytes while exposing user-visible Initial, 0-RTT, ACK, ServerHello, Handshake, and Protected Payload semantics.
notes: Uses the exact QUIC UDP payloads from all 17 packets of the checked-in `quic_example_2.pcap` fixture.
Outer showcase carrier remains synthetic, but protected QUIC bytes are reused exactly so normal import retains the proven structured QUIC/TLS path.

scenarios.name: Rich QUIC Initial with many CRYPTO frames
scenarios.purpose: Purpose-recorded full QUIC flow preserving exact protected UDP payload bytes from a richer multi-CRYPTO Initial capture.
special_packets: QUIC Initial with many CRYPTO frames
notes: Reuses all packets from the full purpose-recorded `QUIC_many_crypto_01.pcap` capture.
Exact UDP payload bytes are preserved while the outer showcase carrier remains synthetic to avoid tuple collisions.

scenarios.name: Rich QUIC Initial and reverse ACK / ServerHello path
scenarios.purpose: Purpose-recorded full QUIC flow preserving exact protected UDP payload bytes from a second richer QUIC capture with repeated reverse Initial and Handshake activity.
special_packets: QUIC Initial with many CRYPTO frames
notes: Reuses all packets from the full purpose-recorded `QUIC_many_crypto_02.pcap` capture.
Exact UDP payload bytes are preserved while the outer showcase carrier remains synthetic to avoid tuple collisions.

scenarios.name: Undecryptable QUIC Initial
scenarios.purpose: Short QUIC Initial scenario that remains coarse/protected with no fabricated plaintext structure.

scenarios.name: Short direct TLS ClientHello flow
scenarios.purpose: Third compact TLS flow with a direct ClientHello/SNI path rather than a long analysis hero.

scenarios.name: Segmented TLS ClientHello with continued SNI
scenarios.purpose: Compact TLS flow where the first ClientHello segment is sufficient for import-time TLS detection, but the SNI bytes arrive only in the second TCP segment and are recovered later by bounded selected-flow reconstruction.
special_packets: TLS ClientHello spanning two TCP segments
SNI located only in the continuation segment
notes: Exact TLS payload segmentation is reused from `tests/data/parsing/tls/tls_sni_in_second_segment_20.pcap`.
Initial import detects `TLS` but leaves Service empty because the SNI is not yet physically present in the first TCP segment.
Selecting/loading the flow allows bounded TCP/TLS reconstruction to recover `edge.microsoft.com`.

scenarios.name: TLS without observed SNI
scenarios.purpose: Compact valid TLS handshake example with structured TLS presentation but no observed SNI because only the server-side handshake packet is present.
notes: This scenario is intentionally described as TLS without observed SNI rather than as a ClientHello that omitted SNI.

scenarios.name: SSH banner hint demo
scenarios.purpose: Short TCP flow demonstrating current SSH banner-based detected-protocol behavior.
notes: Current UI support is hint-oriented rather than a deep SSH parser.

scenarios.name: STUN binding request/response hint demo
scenarios.purpose: Short UDP flow demonstrating current STUN message-shape hint detection.
notes: Current UI support is hint-oriented rather than a deep STUN parser.

scenarios.name: BitTorrent handshake hint demo
scenarios.purpose: Short TCP flow demonstrating current canonical BitTorrent handshake detection.
notes: Current UI support is hint-oriented rather than a deep BitTorrent parser.

scenarios.name: SMTP hint demo
scenarios.purpose: Short TCP flow demonstrating current SMTP greeting/EHLO hint detection.
notes: Counts toward the aggregated Statistics row `Mail protocols`.

scenarios.name: POP3 hint demo
scenarios.purpose: Short TCP flow demonstrating current POP3 greeting/command hint detection.
notes: Counts toward the aggregated Statistics row `Mail protocols`.

scenarios.name: IMAP hint demo
scenarios.purpose: Short TCP flow demonstrating current IMAP greeting/tagged-command hint detection.
notes: Counts toward the aggregated Statistics row `Mail protocols`.

scenarios.name: DHCP hint demo
scenarios.purpose: Short BOOTP/DHCP flow demonstrating current DHCP magic-cookie detection on UDP/67-68.
notes: Current UI support is hint-oriented rather than a deep DHCP parser.

scenarios.name: Settings-gated Possible TLS demo
scenarios.purpose: Opaque TCP/443 flow that stays non-confirmed by default and only surfaces as Possible TLS when the fallback setting is enabled.
notes: Default behavior remains Unknown because `use_possible_tls_quic` is disabled by default.
When `use_possible_tls_quic` is enabled and the capture is reopened/imported, this flow should appear as Possible TLS.

scenarios.name: Settings-gated Possible QUIC demo
scenarios.purpose: Opaque UDP/443 flow that is not a valid QUIC long header and only surfaces as Possible QUIC when the fallback setting is enabled.
notes: Default behavior remains Unknown because `use_possible_tls_quic` is disabled by default.
This is intentionally distinct from `APP-QUIC-NEG-01`, which is still a confirmed QUIC long-header flow.

scenarios.name: Same UDP tuple split by VLAN identity
scenarios.purpose: Two otherwise identical UDP packets intentionally differ only by VLAN identity so default flow grouping keeps them separate.
notes: Manual GUI grouping demo: Ignore VLAN layers when grouping flows should merge these flows.
Primary source semantics validated from `tests/data/parsing/vlan/05_qinq_ipv4_udp.pcap`; scenario is materialized synthetically to produce a clean same-tuple identity pair.

scenarios.name: Same TCP tuple split by MPLS label identity
scenarios.purpose: Two otherwise identical TCP SYN packets intentionally differ only by MPLS label so default grouping keeps them separate.
notes: Manual GUI grouping demo: Ignore MPLS layers when grouping flows should merge these flows.
Primary source semantics validated from `tests/data/parsing/mpls/23_mpls_same_inner_flow_different_labels.pcap`; scenario is materialized synthetically to produce a clean same-tuple identity pair.

scenarios.name: Same inner TCP tuple split by GTP-U TEID
scenarios.purpose: Two GTP-U packets keep the same inner TCP tuple while differing by TEID to demonstrate current identity behavior.
scenarios.expected_protocol_path: EthernetII -> IPv4 -> UDP -> GTP-U -> IPv4 -> TCP
notes: Manual GUI grouping demo: Ignore GTP-U TEIDs when grouping inner flows should merge these flows.

scenarios.name: Same inner TCP tuple split by VXLAN VNI
scenarios.purpose: Two VXLAN packets keep the same inner TCP tuple while differing by VNI to demonstrate identity visibility.
scenarios.expected_protocol_path: EthernetII -> IPv4 -> UDP -> VXLAN -> EthernetII -> IPv4 -> TCP

scenarios.name: Same inner TCP tuple split by Geneve VNI
scenarios.purpose: Two Geneve packets keep the same inner TCP tuple while differing by VNI to demonstrate identity visibility.
scenarios.expected_protocol_path: EthernetII -> IPv4 -> UDP -> Geneve -> EthernetII -> IPv4 -> TCP

scenarios.name: SCTP data packet
scenarios.purpose: Short SCTP scenario proving current user-visible SCTP flow recognition.

scenarios.name: IPv4 AH with inner TCP
scenarios.purpose: Small AH scenario showing that normal import exposes AH plus the inner TCP tuple.

scenarios.name: IPv4 ESP packet
scenarios.purpose: Small ESP scenario showing current normal import exposure of ESP as a recognized protocol flow.

scenarios.name: IPv4-in-IPv4 tunnel packet
scenarios.purpose: Small IP-in-IP scenario showing canonical tunnel path visibility.

scenarios.name: PPPoE session packet
scenarios.purpose: Small PPPoE session scenario proving PPPoE/PPP path visibility.

scenarios.name: PBB packet with inner IPv4/TCP
scenarios.purpose: Small PBB scenario proving provider-bridging path visibility.

scenarios.name: LLC/SNAP packet with IPv4/TCP
scenarios.purpose: Small LLC/SNAP scenario proving 802.3 + LLC path visibility.

scenarios.name: EoIP packet with inner IPv4/TCP
scenarios.purpose: Small EoIP scenario proving current nested GRE/Ethernet visibility.
scenarios.expected_protocol_path: EthernetII -> IPv4 -> GRE -> EthernetII -> IPv4 -> TCP

scenarios.name: IGMP membership report
scenarios.purpose: Short IGMP control scenario showing current detected-protocol and service presentation.

scenarios.name: MPLS pseudowire packet
scenarios.purpose: Small MPLS pseudowire scenario proving current nested Ethernet path visibility.
scenarios.expected_protocol_path: EthernetII -> MPLS -> MPLS -> Pseudowire -> EthernetII -> IPv4 -> TCP

scenarios.name: IPv4 packet with structured options
scenarios.purpose: Short IPv4-options scenario showing current Summary/Bytes support for structured IPv4 options.

scenarios.name: TCP SYN with structured options
scenarios.purpose: Short TCP-options scenario showing current Summary/Bytes support for MSS, SACK Permitted, Timestamps, NOP, and Window Scale.

scenarios.name: ARP request/reply
scenarios.purpose: Simple ARP request/reply pair.

scenarios.name: ICMP control traffic
scenarios.purpose: Echo request/reply plus one useful ICMP error.
notes: Flow protocol-path expectations intentionally follow current app semantics, which stop at IPv4 for this flow.

scenarios.name: TCP reset presentation
scenarios.purpose: Short TCP connection ending in RST for flags presentation.

scenarios.name: Classic-PCAP caplen/origlen distinction
scenarios.purpose: Real caplen/origlen difference for captured/original byte semantics.

scenarios.name: IPv4 fragmentation
scenarios.purpose: Small deterministic IPv4 fragmentation scenario using only currently supported semantics.

scenarios.name: Unrecognized truncated Ethernet bytes
scenarios.purpose: Capture-level unrecognized packet with Packet Summary fallback and Captured Packet byte view.

scenarios.name: MACsec packet-inspection-only unrecognized packet
scenarios.purpose: Unrecognized packet that still exposes structured MACsec packet inspection without forming a normal flow.
notes: This remains packet-inspection-only rather than a normal flow-grouping scenario.

scenarios.name: PPPoE discovery no-flow packet
scenarios.purpose: Unrecognized PPPoE discovery control packet with structured PPPoE packet details but no normal flow identity.

scenarios.name: LLC/SNAP unknown PID no-flow packet
scenarios.purpose: IEEE 802.3 LLC/SNAP packet that reaches SNAP parsing but remains unrecognized because the PID is unsupported.

scenarios.name: MPLS no-flow packet without bottom-of-stack
scenarios.purpose: Unrecognized MPLS packet that still exposes multiple MPLS labels in Packet Details before flow-key extraction stops.

known_limitations: Does not advertise retransmission classification or out-of-order storytelling.
Does not advertise DNS transaction correlation beyond current structured packet/stream presentation.
Does not advertise recursive ICMP quoted-packet deep inspection.
Does not advertise ICMPv6/NDP deep inspection.
Does not advertise deep SCTP Stream semantics.
Does not advertise deep SVCB/HTTPS parsing.

MACsec remains packet-inspection-only in the primary showcase: L2-MACSEC-PACKET-01 is intentionally a no-flow/unrecognized packet with structured Summary/Bytes support rather than a normal recognized flow.
SLL/SLL2 support is intentionally excluded from this primary Ethernet showcase and can live in a separate companion capture later.
validation_smoke_checks: Open the capture and confirm Flows / Analysis / Statistics load without requiring an index.

Open Statistics -> Detected Protocol Hints and confirm all current confirmed application-hint families have at least one representative row: HTTP, TLS, DNS, QUIC, SSH, STUN, BitTorrent, Mail protocols, DHCP, and mDNS.
If `use_possible_tls_quic` is enabled before reopening/importing the capture, confirm HINT-POSSIBLE-TLS-01 and HINT-POSSIBLE-QUIC-01 move from Unknown into Possible TLS / Possible QUIC respectively.
Inspect AN-TLS-BULK-01 for TLS SNI, rate phases, packet-size histogram, inter-arrival histogram, and burst/idle regions.
Inspect AN-GRE-TLS-01 for complex protocol path and nested TLS stream/bytes presentation.

Inspect APP-HTTP-02, APP-HTTP-LARGEBODY-01, APP-DNS-02, APP-TLS-03, APP-TLS-SEGMENTED-01, APP-TLS-NOSNI-01, APP-SSH-01, APP-STUN-01, APP-BITTORRENT-01, APP-SMTP-01, APP-POP3-01, APP-IMAP-01, and APP-DHCP-01 for representative confirmed detected-protocol hint coverage.

Inspect APP-TLS-SEGMENTED-01 and confirm that initial import detects TLS while Service starts empty, then selected-flow reconstruction recovers edge.microsoft.com because the SNI resides only in the second TCP segment.
Inspect APP-MDNS6-01 for compact IPv6 UDP/mDNS/DNS-SD behavior with structured PTR, SRV, TXT, and AAAA presentation.
Inspect APP-QUIC-01, APP-QUIC-MULTICRYPTO-01, APP-QUIC-MULTICRYPTO-02, and APP-QUIC-NEG-01 for compact positive, rich positive, and coarse negative QUIC Initial behavior.
Inspect APP-QUIC-01 packet 1 for Initial/CRYPTO/ClientHello, packet 3 for Initial/0-RTT, one reverse packet for Initial ACK, and packet 13 for ServerHello.
Inspect APP-QUIC-MULTICRYPTO-01 packet 1 for many CRYPTO/PING/PADDING frames plus ClientHello, packet 4 for reverse ServerHello, and later packets for Handshake / Protected Payload.
Inspect APP-QUIC-MULTICRYPTO-02 packet 1 for many CRYPTO/PING/PADDING frames plus ClientHello, packets 3-4 for reverse Initial ACK behavior, and packets 5-6 for reverse ServerHello.
Inspect ID-VLAN-PAIR-01, ID-MPLS-LABEL-01, OVL-GTPU-TEID-01, OVL-VXLAN-VNI-01, and OVL-GENEVE-VNI-01 for identity-tree diversity and manual GUI grouping demonstrations.
Inspect NET-IPV4-OPTIONS-01 and TCP-OPTIONS-01 for current structured options presentation.
Inspect EDGE-SNAPLEN-01 for captured/original length semantics and bounded byte view.
Inspect EDGE-UNREC-01, L2-MACSEC-PACKET-01, L2-PPPOE-DISCOVERY-01, L2-LLCSNAP-UNREC-01, and TUN-MPLS-UNREC-01 for distinct unrecognized-packet reasons, packet-inspection depth, and Bytes behavior.
